inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information: The operation did not have emergency care information such as physician address and phone number for one child who is transported.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: Multiple tubes of diaper rash cream was stored on a shelf accessible to children in the toddler classroom.     Note: The caregiver removed the items from the area during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3807(1))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: Two caregivers need training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Director's Absence - Qualified Caregiver in Charge: Upon arrival, there was no designated qualified caregiver present at the operation in the director's absence.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director's Absence - Qualified Caregiver in Charge (26 TAC §746.1013(a))

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: An updated immunization record is needed for one child enrolled.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Daily Menus - Record Comparable Substitutions: The posted menu showed the children were to be served beef meatballs, white rice, corn, apple  sauce, and milk for lunch. The children were served chicken nuggets, tater tots, fruit cocktail, corn, and wheat bread.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Daily Menus - Record Comparable Substitutions (26 TAC §746.3313(1))

occurrences.finding: Infant Daily Report - Share with Parent: The infant caregiver was not utilizing an infant daily report during today's inspection.     Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Daily Report - Share with Parent (26 TAC §746.2431)

occurrences.finding: No Blocked or Locked Doors as Exits: An exit located on the outdoor play area was blocked as bushes had grown around the exit gate.
occurrences.violation_type_title: No Blocked or Locked Doors as Exits (26 TAC §746.5209(c))

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface: The diaper changing pad in the infant classroom is torn.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface (26 TAC §746.3503(a))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink: A caregiver in the infant classroom uses the handwashing sink for cleaning bottles.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink (26 TAC §746.2419(8))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation: Two caregivers did not have documentation showing orientation training was completed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(1)(A))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: Two caregivers need pediatric CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Complying with Laws and Rules: The operation is not maintaining compliance and has had several repeated deficiencies. Several inspection and follow ups were conducted due to the operations inability to maintain compliance.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Complying with Laws and Rules (26 TAC §746.201(9))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: Brown ceiling tiles were observed in the toddler classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely: The vehicle's 3rd row back seat had 1 seatbelt at the end of the row that would not fasten. The first row's middle seat did not have a fastener for the seatbelt.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely (26 TAC §746.5603(c))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired: During this inspection I observed broken toys on the outdoor play area as well as a torn rug.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired (26 TAC §746.4751(c))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A 22 month old child was left unsupervised in the toddler classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The operations 2024-2025 handbook was reviewed and the following policies are needed:  Preventing and responding to abuse and neglect of children. Procedures for medical emergencies. Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activities.  	Procedures for supporting inclusive services to children with special care needs. Parent rights that are consistent with the rules in Division 5 of the minimum standards.  The Emergency Preparedness Plan did not include: The emergency telephone number that is on file with Child Care Regulation. How the operation will communicate with local authorities and Child Care Regulation. How staff will evacuate and relocate with the essential documentation such as authorization for emergency care for each child in care. The phone number listed for the local Child Care Regulation office needed updating.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: Training Criteria - Certificate: A certificate showing one staff member successfully completed 14 clock hours for the most recent complete training period was not available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Criteria - Certificate (26 TAC §746.1317(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records Maintained: Records were evaluated for six children enrolled and the following was determined:    An admission date is needed for one child.     A statement of special needs is needed for two children.     Updated immunization records is needed for one child.     An address for the emergency contact is needed for one. child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §746.603(a))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Germicidal wipes were stored on a shelf accessible to children in the toddler classroom.       Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: I observed chipped paint on the walls of the toddler classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: During this inspection I observed children on unlabeled nap mats.     Note: This was corrected during inspection. The operation created a nap chart and numbered the napping equipment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))

occurrences.finding: Individual Cot, Bed, or Mat for Each Walking Child Through 4 Years of Age: During this inspection children were observed laying on torn napping equipment.     Note: This was corrected during inspection when the mats were replaced.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Individual Cot, Bed, or Mat for Each Walking Child Through 4 Years of Age (26 TAC §746.4503(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information: During the follow up, the transportation binder showed that 2 children still need emergency medical transport and treatment authorization.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During this inspection a transportation driver from another licensed childcare operation sent a thirteen-year-old child into the building to wait for another child in care. Once the child arrived the two children walked across the parking lot and entered the van where the driver was waiting.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information: The transportation binder was reviewed and showed 11 children needed emergency medical transport and treatment authorization.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The operation is not maintaining compliance and has had several repeated deficiencies. The operation has had repeated deficiencies regarding caregiver responsibilities, including maintaining supervision of all children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During this inspection two children ages 4 and 10 were left unsupervised in a classroom.     During this inspection a caregiver left a group of children ages 3 months, 12 months, and 15 months unsupervised.     During this inspection a caregiver responsible for a group of school age children left the classroom unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on the information obtained, it was determined a caregiver did not demonstrate good judgement when agreeing to pick a child up at a location other than what   was approved by their parent.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - Crossing Street: Based on the information obtained, it was determined a caregiver did not exercise   proper safety precautions when loading a child by agreeing to have the child cross the street   at dismissal
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - Crossing Street (26 TAC §746.5605(2))

occurrences.finding: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System: The sign in and out log was reviewed during this inspection and showed 17 children were signed in however 16 children were present at the operation.     Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A thirteen year old was observed alone in a classroom during this inspection.    During this inspection a three year old left one classroom and went to another.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System: The sign in and out log was reviewed and showed fourteen of fifteen children present were signed in.     Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: A caregiver responsible for a group of children ages 3-13 years old was unaware of the number of children responsible for. The caregiver stated eight were present however nine were counted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Transportation training: The center director is in need of transportation training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Transportation training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(7)(A))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: Training in all special topics is needed for two staff members.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Children's Products- Annual Certification: The annual certification was last completed 01/06/2022.    Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Products- Annual Certification (26 TAC §746.4135(b))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: One caregiver is in need of Pediatric First Aid training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: During this inspection a child did not wash their hands after diapering.     Note: This was corrected at inspection when the child was sent to the hand washing sink to wash their hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The last fire inspection was conducted 12/2021.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: Updated immunization records are needed for two children enrolled.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: One caregiver is in need of Pediatric CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: During this inspection the following was observed:    -The lights in the infant room did not turn on.  -Two lights in the toddler room were out.  -One light in the school age room was out.   -Broken pieces of wood and nails protruding from wood was observed on the playground.   -Wall plates were missing from one outlet in the school age room and one outlet in the toddler room.   -Detached baseboards with protruding nails were observed in the school age room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: No Blocked or Locked Doors as Exits: An exit located on the outdoor play area was blocked as bushes had grown around the exit gate.
occurrences.violation_type_title: No Blocked or Locked Doors as Exits (26 TAC §746.5209(c))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: During this investigation it was determined that cleaning supplies were stored on a shelf, accessible to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: During this investigation, it was determined that a parent was not notified of less serious injuries.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))

occurrences.finding: Operation Open to Parents At All Times: Based on information during this investigation, it was determined that the operation is not open to parents at all times.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Operation Open to Parents At All Times (26 TAC §746.201(7))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children: Based on information obtained during this investigation, it was determined that a caregiver left a group of children unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on information obtained during this investigation, it was determined that a caregiver did not demonstrate good judgment by allowing children to sweep and mop the operation. The caregiver also did not demonstrate good judgment by allowing a child to use a rag containing bleach.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers-Report Suspected Child Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation: Based on the information obtained during this investigation, it was determined that the operation did not report an alleged act of suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers-Report Suspected Child Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation (26 TAC §746.1201(5))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and directors - Pediatric CPR: Based on information obtained, it was determined that a caregiver did not receive Pediatric CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and directors - Pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1301(4)(A))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Drinking Water Available and Served: A supply of drinking water was not available during lunch time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Drinking Water Available and Served (26 TAC §746.3301(f))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired: The outdoor play area used by children was not maintained. Inspector observed the following during this inspection:      -Broken pieces of glass.    -Broken toys.  -Trash/Debris   -The grass was in need of cutting.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired (26 TAC §746.4751(c))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation: Two staff members needed orientation training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation (26 TAC §746.1301(1)(A))

occurrences.finding: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely: One of the side doors on the van where children enter and exit does not open.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely (26 TAC §746.5603(c))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records Maintained: Records were evaluated for six children in care and the following was determined:    Two needed an updated immunization record.   One needed a health statement.   One needed a food allergy statement.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §746.603(a))

occurrences.finding: Inspect Fire Extinguishers Monthly: The operation did not have documentation showing the fire extinguishers were inspected monthly.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Inspect Fire Extinguishers Monthly (26 TAC §746.5307(a))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: During this inspection I observed part of the door frame of the toddler class coming apart from the wall area. Nails were observed protruding from the separated piece of wood.     During this inspection I observed trash and other debris on the outdoor playground.   Note: The operation removed the items from the playground during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements: One staff members needed documentation showing how they meet the minimum education qualifications.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements (26 TAC §746.901(2))

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021 data from February 23, 2022, revealed that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021 by February 22, 2022, as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The last fire inspection was conducted on 11/10/2020.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: I observed children sleeping on unlabeled nap mats in the toddler classroom. I also observed unlabeled napping equipment in the classroom.    Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))
